trigger_criteria: Read traffic outnumbers write traffic >20x with complex aggregated reporting views
decision_rationale: Optimizing read models with denormalized read stores prevents expensive joins from impacting OLTP write latencies.

trigger_criteria: Transaction spanning 2 or more microservices or distinct databases
decision_rationale: 2PC creates high latency and network-partition vulnerability; Sagas use local transactions with compensating rollbacks.

trigger_criteria: High-volume event ingestion, write latency <10ms, append-only logs
decision_rationale: Avoid table-level or row-level lock contention during writes; buffer and write append-only outbox records.

trigger_criteria: Rapidly growing application with autonomous feature squads touching the same codebase
decision_rationale: Horizontal layers create merge conflicts and cross-cutting coupling; vertical slices keep changes co-located and isolated.

trigger_criteria: Large legacy monolith that cannot be rewritten in a single big-bang release
decision_rationale: Strangler fig allows incremental value delivery and side-by-side verification, minimizing operational risk.

trigger_criteria: Distinct web, mobile, and third-party partners requiring tailored response shapes and security
decision_rationale: BFF prevents over-fetching on mobile networks and isolates internal microservice refactoring from public clients.

trigger_criteria: Heavy integration with volatile third-party ERP, CRM, or payment gateway APIs
decision_rationale: Anti-Corruption Layer translates vendor concepts at the boundary, ensuring vendor schema changes don't break domain logic.

trigger_criteria: Financial, healthcare, or regulatory requirement demanding complete time-travel auditability
decision_rationale: Event sourcing guarantees that every state mutation is captured as an immutable business event that can be replayed.
